title: Daemon stream command identity and server timing observations
description: Objective: make the daemon's event-stream seam emit the command/run identity and the daemon-observed timing readings that every downstream timing and effort attribution needs, without inventing either. Deliverable: StreamEvent and WireEvent carry the command identity (commandId, and the actor/principal plus session/run identity the source actually provides) and DISTINCT daemon-observed timestamps, each bound to an explicit observer so no later layer compares two clocks silently. SPIDR slice 1 of 3 from parent task-1eeb2dccce204671b442704cd60b38ad; siblings are the live consumer edge and the decision-effort observations. MEASURED AT HEAD 6ffb4fe (re-measure, this WILL be stale): apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream-contract.ts:30 StreamEvent is exactly {aggregateId, committedAt, eventId, eventType, globalPosition} and WireEvent is the same five with globalPosition as string - no commandId, no actor, no session, one timestamp only. packages/store/src/command-decision-test-helpers.ts:85 shows domain_events HAS a command_id column NOT NULL with an FK to command_receipts, and packages/store/src/outbox-relay/transactional-outbox-relay.ts:54 queries domain_events BY command_id, so command identity exists at the source. OPEN RISK THIS TASK MUST RESOLVE FIRST: event-stream-contract.ts states in its own header comment that the store subscription surface is deliberately NOT imported and that the daemon does not own packages/store. If the subscription read page cannot surface command_id without editing @moe/store, do NOT edit it - report blocked and name a store task. NOT in scope: control-room, client, render or human timing, focus/attention/effort records, benchmark statistics or thresholds. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: StreamEvent and WireEvent carry the command identity (commandId plus the actor/principal and session/run identity the source genuinely provides) alongside the existing five fields, and every identity value is COPIED from the source - no layer synthesizes, defaults or derives one.

Daemon-observed timing readings are distinct and each names its observer explicitly; a server-emitted reading is never collapsed into a server-committed one, and the wire carries enough observer/clock binding that a consumer can tell which clock produced each reading.

An event whose source lacks an identity or a reading yields the exact stable UNKNOWN/absent code plus exact layer at the seam - never an empty string, a zero timestamp, a fabricated id, or a silently dropped field.

Seam refusals stay separate from forwarded store refusals exactly as today: EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES remains closed and every frame still names its layer, so a seam refusal is never mistaken for a store refusal.

Refusal tests pin the exact code AND layer; generated identity/observation cases assert a nonzero exact cardinality, and a mutation that drops an identity field from the wire mapping or collapses two readings turns a named test red.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck exits 0.
taskRails: Do not edit packages/store. The stream contract deliberately does not own that package; if command identity cannot reach the seam without a store change, report blocked and name a store task instead of reaching across the boundary.
Do not collapse distinct daemon readings into one timestamp; a server-emitted reading is not a server-committed reading.
Never compare or subtract timestamps from different clocks at this layer. This task emits readings with observer binding; it computes no durations.
Instrumentation is observational and grants no authority or evidence strength; identity fields are copied, never minted.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400; the cap is per file. event-stream-contract.ts is 177 and event-stream.ts is 182 today.

implementationPlan.description: Extend the wire vocabulary in apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream-contract.ts, keeping the module's central invariant intact: StreamEvent is a STRUCTURAL VIEW of the store page and a real StoredEvent must stay assignable to it. That constraint decides the whole design — StreamEvent may gain ONLY what the source provides (`commandId: string`, and `decisionTrace?` with its six fields typed as plain `string`, which a StoredEvent's literal-typed requestIdentityVersion satisfies), and must NOT gain a daemon-observed reading, because StoredEvent has none and requiring one would break assignability and force the store edit rail 1 forbids. The daemon-observed reading is added by the seam during encode and therefore lives on WireEvent only. Publish on WireEvent: an identity block carrying commandId plus actor/principal and session/run as explicit known-or-unknown values, and TWO distinct observation values. Add three new CLOSED frozen vocabularies with `(typeof)[number]` types: observers (DAEMON_SEAM, STORE_LEDGER), clocks (DAEMON_WALL_CLOCK, STORE_COMMIT_CLOCK), and unknown codes (an identity-not-provided code and a reading-not-provided code). An unknown value is `{known: false, code, layer: EVENT_STREAM_LAYER}` and a known one carries its value; an observation is `{observer, clock, reading}`. EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES MUST stay byte-identical at its current three members — an absent identity is not a frame refusal, and DoD 4 requires that vocabulary to stay closed and separate. Add the `SeamObserver` port type (`{ now(): string }`) the next step injects. Comment WHY the two readings must never be collapsed or subtracted here. Measure the file afterwards: 177 + roughly 55 lines lands near 232, under the 250 target; if it crosses, split the observation vocabulary into event-stream-observation.ts plus its one-line `.js` bridge rather than trimming the comments.

CONTRACT CHANGES:
- StreamEvent gains `commandId: string` and optional `decisionTrace?` with the six fields typed as plain `string`. Typed plain deliberately: the store's `requestIdentityVersion` is a literal type and a literal IS assignable to `string`, not the reverse. `decisionTrace` stays OPTIONAL because `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` is on and StoredEvent declares it optional — a required field here would break assignability and force exactly the store edit rail 1 forbids. Header comment states why no daemon reading may live on StreamEvent.
- WireEvent gains `identity`, `ledgerObservation`, `seamObservation`.
- New closed frozen vocabularies with `(typeof)[number]` types: EVENT_STREAM_OBSERVERS (DAEMON_SEAM, STORE_LEDGER), EVENT_STREAM_CLOCKS (DAEMON_WALL_CLOCK, STORE_COMMIT_CLOCK), EVENT_STREAM_UNKNOWN_CODES (EVENT_STREAM_IDENTITY_NOT_PROVIDED, EVENT_STREAM_READING_NOT_PROVIDED).
- `WireValue = WireKnownValue | WireUnknownValue`; unknown is `{code, known: false, layer}`, known is `{known: true, value}`. `WireObservation = {clock, observer, reading}`. `WireEventIdentity = {commandId, principal, run, session}`. `SeamObserver = {now(): string}`.
- The comment explaining why the two readings must never be collapsed or subtracted is on the observer vocabulary: they are different clocks in different processes, so their difference is a real interval plus an unknown offset, not a duration.

Assertions: (1) ASSIGNABILITY GUARD — declare a fixture typed as `StoredEvent` imported type-only from the bare `@moe/store` root (allowed: that is the store's public root, not the subscription surface the header forbids importing) and assert at compile time that it is assignable to StreamEvent, so a future widening that breaks the structural view fails the typecheck instead of silently forcing a store change. (2) IDENTITY IS COPIED, NEVER MINTED — for a page of events, every wire commandId is `===` the source commandId and every principal value is `===` the source decisionTrace principal; assert a hand-written exact case cardinality over the generated ledger, not merely that the array is non-empty. (3) UNKNOWN, NOT EMPTY — an event without decisionTrace yields the identity-not-provided code at layer SEAM for actor/principal; session/run yield that same code for EVERY event because the source provides neither today; an event whose committedAt is missing yields the reading-not-provided code at layer SEAM. Pin code AND layer on each, and assert the emitted value is never `""`, never 0, never a synthesized id, and that the field is present rather than dropped. (4) TWO DISTINCT READINGS — each wire event carries a STORE_LEDGER/STORE_COMMIT_CLOCK observation whose reading is `===` committedAt, and a DAEMON_SEAM/DAEMON_WALL_CLOCK observation from the injected observer; assert the two are separate fields with different observer and clock tags and that neither is derived from the other. (5) ONE FRAME, ONE SEAM OBSERVATION — with a ten-event page, the counting observer records EXACTLY one call, and all ten events carry that identical reading; a per-event clock call would manufacture precision the seam does not have and invite a consumer to diff two readings from one clock. No test may subtract or compare two readings. (6) VOCABULARY CLOSURE — EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES still equals its exact three members, and the new unknown-code vocabulary is disjoint from it. Run and record the RED.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the mapping in apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream.ts. Add a module-level frozen default SeamObserver that reads the daemon wall clock and returns a canonical timestamp string, and thread an OPTIONAL third parameter `observer: SeamObserver = <default>` through readEventPage into pageFrame. Optional and last is deliberate: apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts:116 calls `readEventPage(options.subscriptions, request)` and a required parameter would ripple into the listener options type and every listener/adapter test fixture, so the blast radius stays inside this seam. Take the seam reading ONCE per page encode and stamp every event in that page with it. In `wireEvent`, copy commandId straight from the source event; map decisionTrace's principal/actor to a known value when the trace is present and to the identity-not-provided unknown when it is not; emit session and run as that same unknown for every event, because step 1 measured that the source provides neither — emitting the field as an explicit unknown rather than omitting it is what lets the two sibling tasks see the gap instead of inheriting a silent hole. Build the STORE_LEDGER observation from committedAt, falling back to the reading-not-provided unknown when it is absent or not a usable timestamp, and the DAEMON_SEAM observation from the observer reading, falling back the same way if the observer returns nothing usable — never a zero timestamp and never the other clock's value. Freeze every new sub-record exactly as the existing wire helpers do. Compute no duration, compare no two readings, and derive nothing: this module emits readings and copies identities. Re-measure the file against the 250 target.

THAT MOVE ALSO DELETED A LATENT IMPORT CYCLE, which is the part worth reviewing. Before: observation.ts type-imported EVENT_STREAM_LAYER from the contract while the contract re-exported observation's values — safe only because the type import erased. Once the builders needed that layer as a RUNTIME value, the cycle would have become real. So `EVENT_STREAM_LAYER` now LIVES in event-stream-observation.ts and the contract re-exports it. The contract's public surface is unchanged (it still exports EVENT_STREAM_LAYER by name, and index.ts is untouched by this), and observation.ts now imports nothing from the contract but the `StreamEvent` type. The value edge runs strictly one way, contract -> observation.

THE MAPPING:
- `DEFAULT_SEAM_OBSERVER` is a frozen module-level `{now: () => new Date().toISOString()}`; `readEventPage(port, request, observer = DEFAULT_SEAM_OBSERVER)` keeps the parameter optional AND last, so http-listener.ts:116's two-argument call is untouched — verified by running http-listener.test.ts green.
- ONE READING PER FRAME: `observer.now()` is called once inside `pageFrame` and the same string is stamped onto every event via `wireEvent(event, seamReading)`. It is NOT called for REFUSED or CURSOR_GAP frames, which take no reading at all.
- `identityOf` copies `commandId` straight off the source, maps `decisionTrace.principalId` to a known value when the trace exists and to EVENT_STREAM_IDENTITY_NOT_PROVIDED when it does not, and emits `session`/`run` as that same not-provided unknown on every event. Nothing synthesizes, defaults or derives an identity.
- `readingOf(value: unknown)` is deliberately typed `unknown`, not `string`: it accepts a reading only when `typeof value === "string" && value !== ""`, so BOTH an absent reading and a blank one fall back to EVENT_STREAM_READING_NOT_PROVIDED. Never `""`, never a zero timestamp, and never the other clock's value — the two degenerate directions are covered by separate tests, so an unusable ledger timestamp cannot silently borrow the seam reading or vice versa.
- Every new sub-record is `Object.freeze`d, matching the existing wire helpers.
- NO duration is computed and no two readings are compared anywhere in the module. The seam emits readings with provenance attached; that is all it does.
